subject: Biology
title: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
summary: DNA is the genetic material in most organisms (RNA in some viruses). Watson and Crick (1953) proposed the double helix: two antiparallel polynucleotide strands with A=T and G≡C pairing (Chargaff's rule).

Griffith (transformation), Avery–MacLeod–McCarty (transforming principle is DNA) and Hershey–Chase (bacteriophage, ³²P vs ³⁵S) proved DNA is the genetic material. Meselson and Stahl proved semi-conservative replication.
The central dogma: DNA → (transcription) → RNA → (translation) → protein. The genetic code is triplet, degenerate, universal (nearly) and non-overlapping.
Gene expression is regulated — the lac operon of E. coli is the classic example. The Human Genome Project and DNA fingerprinting apply this knowledge.

formulas.name: Chargaff's rule
formulas.formula: A = T, G = C;  (A + G) = (T + C);  purines = pyrimidines
formulas.mistake: Does not apply to single-stranded DNA or RNA.

formulas.name: B-DNA dimensions
formulas.formula: diameter 2 nm;  pitch 3.4 nm;  10 bp per turn;  0.34 nm between bp;  right-handed, antiparallel (5′→3′ and 3′→5′)

formulas.name: Length of DNA
formulas.formula: length = number of bp × 0.34 nm;  human diploid ≈ 6.6 × 10⁹ bp → ≈ 2.2 m

formulas.name: Genome sizes
formulas.formula: φ × 174: 5386 nucleotides;  λ phage: 48,502 bp;  E. coli: 4.6 × 10⁶ bp;  human haploid: 3.3 × 10⁹ bp
formulas.note: Exam questions often use an E. coli DNA length of 1.36 mm, which works out to 4 × 10⁶ bp.

formulas.name: Packaging
formulas.formula: nucleosome = histone octamer (positively charged, rich in lysine and arginine) + ~200 bp DNA;  beads-on-string → chromatin fibre;  euchromatin (loose, active) vs heterochromatin (dense, inactive)

formulas.name: Key experiments
formulas.formula: Griffith 1928: S and R strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae — transformation;  Avery, MacLeod, McCarty 1944: DNA is the transforming principle;  Hershey–Chase 1952: ³²P (DNA) entered bacteria, ³⁵S (protein) did not

formulas.name: Replication
formulas.formula: semi-conservative (Meselson–Stahl 1958, ¹⁵N in E. coli; Taylor in Vicia faba);  DNA polymerase works 5′→3′;  leading strand continuous, lagging strand discontinuous (Okazaki fragments joined by DNA ligase);  starts at origin of replication

formulas.name: Transcription unit
formulas.formula: promoter (upstream) — structural gene — terminator;  template strand 3′→5′; coding strand 5′→3′ (same sequence as RNA, with T instead of U)

formulas.name: RNA polymerases (eukaryotes)
formulas.formula: RNA pol I → rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S);  RNA pol II → hnRNA (precursor of mRNA);  RNA pol III → tRNA, 5S rRNA, snRNA

formulas.name: Processing of hnRNA
formulas.formula: splicing (introns removed, exons joined);  capping (methyl guanosine triphosphate at 5′ end);  tailing (poly-A tail at 3′ end)

formulas.name: Genetic code
formulas.formula: triplet (64 codons, 61 code for amino acids);  start AUG (methionine);  stop UAA, UAG, UGA;  unambiguous, degenerate, universal (some exceptions), commaless
formulas.note: George Gamow, a physicist, argued that 4 bases must code for 20 amino acids, so the code should be a triplet (4³ = 64 codons). Khorana's chemical synthesis of RNA with defined base combinations, Nirenberg's cell-free protein-synthesis system and Ochoa's enzyme (polynucleotide phosphorylase) helped decipher it.

formulas.name: Translation
formulas.formula: ribosome (small subunit binds mRNA); tRNA (adapter, clover-leaf; anticodon) carries amino acids (charging/aminoacylation);  peptide bond formed by 23S rRNA (ribozyme) in bacteria;  UTRs at both ends

formulas.name: Lac operon
formulas.formula: i (repressor gene) — p (promoter) — o (operator) — z (β-galactosidase), y (permease), a (transacetylase);  lactose (inducer) inactivates repressor → genes transcribed
formulas.note: Negative regulation: the repressor turns the operon off.

formulas.name: Human Genome Project facts
formulas.formula: 3164.7 million bp;  about 30,000 genes (far fewer than the earlier estimates of 80,000–1,40,000);  average gene 3000 bases (dystrophin largest, 2.4 million bases);  less than 2% codes for proteins;  chromosome 1 most genes (2968), Y fewest (231);  SNPs ~1.4 million locations

formulas.name: DNA fingerprinting
formulas.formula: uses VNTRs (minisatellites, repetitive DNA) — Southern blotting with labelled VNTR probe (Alec Jeffreys);  applications: forensics, paternity, population diversity

examples.title: Hershey–Chase
examples.problem: Bacteria infected by phage with ³⁵S-labelled protein: where is the radioactivity after centrifugation?
examples.solution: In the supernatant (with the phage coats), not in the bacteria — showing that protein does not enter the bacteria; DNA (³²P) does.

examples.title: mRNA from coding strand
examples.solution: 5′-AUGCAU-3′ — same as the coding strand with U in place of T.

topics.title: RNA world
topics.explain: RNA was the first genetic material; it can act as a catalyst (ribozyme) and is reactive and unstable. DNA evolved from RNA with chemical changes (2′-OH absent, thymine instead of uracil) that make it more stable. Being double-stranded with complementary strands, DNA also resists change by evolving repair mechanisms.

topics.title: Properties of genetic material
topics.explain: It must replicate, be chemically and structurally stable, allow slow changes (mutation) for evolution and express itself as Mendelian characters.

topics.title: Transcription in bacteria
topics.explain: One RNA polymerase makes all RNAs. Initiation needs the σ (sigma) factor; termination needs the ρ (rho) factor. Transcription and translation can happen together because there is no nuclear membrane.

topics.title: Split genes
topics.explain: Eukaryotic genes have coding exons interrupted by non-coding introns; introns are removed by splicing. Monocistronic genes are mostly eukaryotic; polycistronic genes are mostly bacterial.

topics.title: Mutations and the code
topics.explain: Point mutations change a single base (e.g. sickle-cell). Insertion or deletion of one or two bases shifts the reading frame (frameshift); three bases add or remove one amino acid without shifting the frame.

topics.title: Methodology of HGP
topics.explain: Expressed sequence tags (identifying expressed genes) and sequence annotation (sequencing the whole genome). DNA was cloned into BAC and YAC vectors, sequenced with automated sequencers (Sanger method) and assembled by computer.
